# Drag-end focus restore fires before the dragged item is visible again

## Context

The hosted `e2e-brain` tier reds `WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL.spec.mjs:327` (the #20020 → #20021 repair) on two of the last three shard-9 runs — dev `8eacfb49f2` and PR #20051's head `92e67a589e`, failed and retry alike; green on dev `e2f77dd0fb` — with the end state the cut steward read from the retained trace (#20022, comment 6365360273): after the drop the strip holds the **unfocused** partition for the whole 10 s, no focus-gated rail, Undo disabled, no console or page error. Locally the spec is green. The steward's cut handover left the diagnosis lane open and unowned; this ticket is the diagnosis by code read, the reproduction is AC-1/AC-2.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-10-23 13:3xZ (#20056 … #19147); no equivalent. A2A claim sweep (last 30 messages, all read states): no claim. Memory Core rationale sweep: the #20020 diagnosis treats the restore as always landing — the 150 ms `initDomEvents` window it found sits downstream of a restore that happened.

## The Problem

After a pointer drag of a tab the engine hands focus back to the dragged button (#19281): hiding the original at drag start moves the browser's focus to the body, and the terminal is meant to give it back. `SortZone#processDragEnd` re-shows the dragged original by writing `visibility: null` into its `wrapperStyle`, waits a fixed 30 ms, then calls `focus()`. The re-show is an ordinary vdom update — asynchronous across the worker boundary and not awaited. When the App worker → main round trip takes longer than 30 ms (the hosted tier under ten shards; a seat under load) `focus()` reaches an element that is still `visibility: hidden`. A hidden element is not focusable, so the call is a no-op and nothing retries: focus stays on the body, the strip never regains it, the rail never reveals, the partition stays the unfocused one — the trace's end state. A person under the same load loses keyboard focus to the body after every tab drag.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:643-647` — the re-show (`style.visibility = null; me.dragComponent.wrapperStyle = style`), unawaited.
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:689` — `await me.timeout(30)`; `:691-694` — the restore `dragFocusOwner.focus(id, false, true, 'pointer')`, guarded only by `isDestroyed`.
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:930` — `dragFocusOwner` captured from `draggedItem.containsFocus` at drag start. The capture is not the race: `src/manager/Focus.mjs:162` `onFocusin` enters focus synchronously on the focusin message, which precedes the drag-start message in DOM order.
- `src/component/Base.mjs:1082` (`afterSetWrapperStyle`) → `:2026` (`updateStyle`) → `:2038` (`update()`): a `wrapperStyle` change reaches the DOM through a round trip, not a frame.
- The spec: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL.spec.mjs:137` sets the mouse sensor's delay to 0, `:221` releases at the origin, `:327` is the predicate that needs `containsFocus` and `contextualActionsVisible` on the header before the partition can settle.

## The Fix

Make the restore wait for the re-show instead of for a clock: in `processDragEnd`, await the dragged component's update (`promiseUpdate()` on `me.dragComponent`, or the owner's when the child update merges into the owner's in-flight one) before the frame wait and the `focus()` call; keep the 30 ms frame wait the overflow drain relies on after it. No new config, no new timing constant. The builder checks that `Overflow#scheduleSortDragProjection`'s drain ordering (`sortZone.dragEndActive`) still holds — the await moves the restore later, never earlier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 (red-first, deterministic): a unit arm on `SortZone#processDragEnd` in which the dragged component's update resolves later than 30 ms (a stubbed `promiseUpdate`/`update`, or a delayed `Neo.applyDeltas`) asserts that `focus()` runs after the re-show has landed — red on dev at the merge-base, green at head.
- [ ] AC-2 (red-first, the specimen): `WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL.spec.mjs`'s gesture with the page's main thread throttled through CDP (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, the rate calibrated on the seat until the base reproduces the trace's end state) is red at the merge-base and green at head; the throttle lives in that arm, never in the spec's default run.
- [ ] AC-3 (post-merge): the shard carrying `WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL` is green on three consecutive hosted `e2e-brain` runs on dev (gate 2's runs count).

## Out of Scope

- The 150 ms `Mixin.DomEvents#initDomEvents` window between the revealed actions' mount and their ResizeObserver (#20020's repair owns it).
- Hover-mode reveals (`showOnHover`), cross-window drags (the `isWindowDragging` / `isRemoteDragging` paths), and a main-thread focus retry in `DomAccess` (broader than this defect).
- The spec's oracle (#20020 / #20021): it is right to demand the focused-extent partition and must not be loosened to pass.

## Avoided Traps

- Raising the 30 ms wait: another clock, the same race one notch further out.
- Having the spec focus the strip after the drop, or polling `document.activeElement` into place: test setup hiding a product defect (the gate-3 walk's lesson behind #20046 — specs that focus the pane as setup never see the unfocused path).
- Reading the hosted red as an oracle defect: the end state is a product state a user reaches under load.
